items.title: Amaravati capital & Polavaram — 2026 status
items.body:
**In one line.** Where Andhra Pradesh's capital stands in 2026 and how far its biggest irrigation project has reached.

**Why it is asked.** The capital's legal status and the Polavaram timeline are the single most repeated AP current-affairs themes, and the exact dates are favourite single-fact questions.

**Amaravati (the capital).** The **AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act, 2026** gave Amaravati permanent legal status as the **sole capital**, ending the earlier 'three-capitals' confusion (the old plan had split functions between Amaravati, Visakhapatnam and Kurnool). Parliament passed it in the 2026 Budget session and President Droupadi Murmu signed it on **6 April 2026**; it amended **Section 5(2)** of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014. Amaravati is also getting the **Quantum Valley Tech Park** (2026), built with **IBM, TCS and IIT Madras**, to house India's largest quantum computer.

**Polavaram Project (on the Godavari river).** This is a multipurpose national irrigation project. Its **new diaphragm wall** (the underground barrier that stops water seeping beneath the dam) was **completed on 2 April 2026**, after which the **Earth-Cum-Rock-Fill (ECRF) dam** — a dam built from layers of earth and rock — began. The reservoir's **Full Reservoir Level (FRL)** is 150 feet above mean sea level and the spillway can pass about 36 lakh cusecs.

| Item | 2026 status |
|---|---|
| Amaravati | Sole capital by statute (Act 2026) |
| Quantum Valley | IBM + TCS + IIT Madras |
| Polavaram diaphragm wall | Completed 2 Apr 2026 |
| Polavaram ECRF dam | Works commenced |

**Don't confuse.** The *diaphragm wall* was completed in April 2026; the *ECRF dam* only then began — the dam is not yet finished. **Remember it:** Amaravati assent and the Polavaram wall both fall in early April 2026.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- AP Reorganization (Amendment) Act, 2026 made Amaravati the sole capital; President's assent 6 April 2026.
- The Act amended Section 5(2) of the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014.
- Amaravati Quantum Valley Tech Park (2026): IBM, TCS, IIT Madras — India's largest quantum computer.
- Polavaram new diaphragm wall completed 2 April 2026; ECRF dam works began.
- Polavaram is on the Godavari; FRL 150 ft, spillway ~36 lakh cusecs.

items.title: AP welfare schemes & agriculture (2025–26)
items.body:
**In one line.** The welfare and farm programmes the Andhra Pradesh government is running in 2025-26.

**Why it is asked.** Scheme names, their beneficiaries and launch dates are classic one-mark questions, and examiners like to swap one scheme's benefit for another's.

The ruling alliance is the **NDA (National Democratic Alliance)** made of the **TDP (Telugu Desam Party), JSP (Jana Sena Party) and BJP (Bharatiya Janata Party)**, with Chief Minister **N. Chandrababu Naidu** (in office from June 2024). Its headline promise is the **'Super Six'** set of welfare guarantees: student and parent support (**Thalliki Vandanam**), subsidised cooking gas (**Deepam-2**), farmer income support (**Annadata Sukhibhava**), women's assistance (**Adabidda Nidhi**), a youth allowance, and free bus travel for women.

**Rythanna Meekosam** (launched **24 November 2025**) is a farmer-empowerment programme built on a **Five-Point Formula**: water security, demand-based cultivation, adoption of farm technology, more food processing, and government support. In plain terms, it tells farmers what crops are in demand, backs them with drones and precision spraying, and promises price support for tobacco, mango, onion and coconut. At its launch, **PM-Kisan Annadata Sukhibhava** was reported to have paid out **over ₹3,200 crore to more than 68 lakh farmers**.

**Remember it:** 'Super Six' = the six election guarantees; Rythanna Meekosam = the farm programme on the Five-Point Formula.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- 'Super Six' = flagship welfare guarantees of the TDP–JSP–BJP government (from June 2024).
- Super Six includes Thalliki Vandanam, Deepam-2, Annadata Sukhibhava, Adabidda Nidhi, youth allowance, free bus travel for women.
- Rythanna Meekosam launched 24 Nov 2025 on a Five-Point Formula for agriculture.
- PM-Kisan Annadata Sukhibhava disbursed over ₹3,200 crore to 68+ lakh farmers.
- Rythanna Meekosam procures tobacco, mango, onion, coconut and promotes drones/agri-tech.

items.title: AP investment leadership & industry (FY26)
items.body:
**In one line.** Why Andhra Pradesh led India on new investment proposals in 2025-26 and the summit that showcased it.

**Why it is asked.** The investment-ranking share and the CII summit venue/host are high-frequency facts, and the ordering of states is a common 'match the percentage' trap.

In the first nine months of **FY26 (April-December 2025)** — FY26 means the financial year running April 2025 to March 2026 — **Andhra Pradesh topped** India's proposed-investment rankings with about **25.3%** of the ₹26.6 lakh crore proposed nationwide, ahead of **Odisha (13.1%)** and **Maharashtra (12.8%)**; the top three together held 51.2% (Bank of Baroda report). National proposals rose 11.5% over the previous year, helped by higher capital spending, lower taxes and **GST 2.0** (the 2025 round of Goods and Services Tax rate cuts).

The **30th CII Partnership Summit 2025** (14-15 November 2025) was held at the **Andhra University Grounds, Visakhapatnam**. **CII** is the Confederation of Indian Industry; the summit was organised with **DPIIT** (the Department for Promotion of Industry and Internal Trade) and the AP government, and inaugurated by **Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan**. It drew 2,500+ delegates from 77 countries on the theme **'Technology, Trust, and Trade'**, with priority sectors of **green hydrogen, semiconductors and precision medicine**. AP also handles about **60% of India's marine-product (seafood) exports**.

**Don't confuse.** AP was 1st for *proposed* investment share (25.3%); Odisha and Maharashtra followed — do not read Odisha's 13.1% as a rank-1 figure.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- AP ranked 1st for proposed investments in FY26 (Apr–Dec 2025) with ~25.3% share.
- Odisha (13.1%) and Maharashtra (12.8%) followed; top-3 = 51.2%.
- 30th CII Partnership Summit 2025 held at Visakhapatnam, 14–15 Nov 2025; VP C. P. Radhakrishnan inaugurated.
- Summit theme: 'Technology, Trust, and Trade'; focus on green hydrogen, semiconductors, precision medicine.
- AP accounts for about 60% of India's marine product exports.

items.title: AP infrastructure milestones (2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** Three big transport and water projects that reached milestones in Andhra Pradesh in 2026.

**Why it is asked.** Opening dates and headquarters of new infrastructure are easy single-fact questions, and the two 'Alluri Sitarama Raju' names (airport vs district) are a planted trap.

| Project (full form) | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| **South Coast Railway (SCoR)** zone | New railway zone began working, headquartered at **Visakhapatnam**, on **1 June 2026** | India's newest railway zone; HQ city is a favourite one-mark fact |
| **Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram** | Commercial flights began on **17 August 2026** | New greenfield airport serving the north-coastal region near Visakhapatnam |
| **Veligonda Project** | Inaugurated in **August 2026** | Lift-irrigation scheme serving Prakasam, Nellore and Kadapa |

SCoR was announced in 2019 and is India's newest railway zone. The Bhogapuram greenfield airport is named after freedom fighter **Alluri Sitarama Raju**. The Veligonda project draws Krishna-basin water through the Nallamala hills for the Rayalaseema and south-coastal belt.

**Don't confuse.** 'Alluri Sitarama Raju' is both the name of the **Bhogapuram airport** and the name of a **district**; a question may test whether you know which is being described.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- South Coast Railway zone operational 1 June 2026; headquarters Visakhapatnam.
- Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport (Bhogapuram) opened commercially 17 August 2026.
- Bhogapuram airport is named after freedom fighter Alluri Sitarama Raju.
- Veligonda Project inaugurated August 2026; serves Prakasam, Nellore, Kadapa.
- SCoR was announced in 2019 and is India's newest railway zone.

items.title: AP governance & administrative structure (2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** Who runs Andhra Pradesh in 2026 and how the state is divided for administration.

**Why it is asked.** The district count and the local-body numbers change often, so examiners test the latest figures; the 26-vs-28 district jump is the classic trap.

**Leadership.** Chief Minister **N. Chandrababu Naidu** (TDP); Deputy CM **Konidela Pawan Kalyan** (Jana Sena Party); capital **Amaravati**; the ruling alliance is the **NDA (TDP-JSP-BJP)**, in office since June 2024.

**How the state is divided.** The **4 April 2022 reorganisation raised districts from 13 to 26**; this was later increased to **28** (adding Polavaram and Markapuram districts) from 31 December 2025. The state covers **162,975 sq km** (India's 7th-largest) with a long Bay of Bengal coast.

**Local bodies (2026).** There are 123 **urban local bodies (ULBs)** — a ULB is a city or town council: **17 municipal corporations, 88 municipalities and 18 nagar panchayats**. The rural tier has **28 zilla parishads** (district councils, effective 25 September 2026), **676 mandal parishads** and **13,351 gram panchayats** (village councils). About **8,139.89 sq km** is notified as protected area.

**Remember it:** districts went 13 → 26 (April 2022) → 28 (end-2025); zilla parishads reached 28 only on 25 September 2026.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- CM Chandrababu Naidu (TDP); Dy CM Pawan Kalyan (JSP); capital Amaravati; NDA (TDP–JSP–BJP).
- AP had 26 districts after the 4 April 2022 reorganisation, raised to 28 (Polavaram, Markapuram) from end-2025; area 162,975 sq km (7th largest).
- 2026 urban local bodies: 17 municipal corporations, 88 municipalities, 18 nagar panchayats.
- 2026 rural tier: 28 zilla parishads (from 25 Sep 2026), 676 mandal parishads, 13,351 gram panchayats.
- About 8,139.89 sq km of AP is notified protected area.

items.title: AP persons, awards, sports & S&T hubs
items.body:
**In one line.** The people, awards, sports result and science hubs from Andhra Pradesh in 2025-26.

**Why it is asked.** 'Who won / who was honoured / where is it located' are quick-recall questions that reward exact names and places.

**People and awards.** Deputy CM **Pawan Kalyan** was inducted (January 2026) into Japan's **Takeda Shingen Clan** and honoured as **'Tiger of Martial Arts'** — the first Telugu-speaking inductee from outside Japan (Fifth Dan rank). In the **Padma Awards 2026**, **Garimella Balakrishna Prasad** (posthumous), from AP, was recognised in the field of **Art**.

**Sports.** **Surya Charishma Tamiri** (AP) won the Women's Singles title at the **87th Senior National Badminton Championships** at **Vijayawada** (December 2025), beating Tanvi Patri.

**Science, defence and space hubs.** The **NSTL** — the Naval Science and Technological Laboratory of the **DRDO** (Defence Research and Development Organisation) at Visakhapatnam — unveiled a man-portable autonomous underwater system (November 2025). Visakhapatnam also hosts the Eastern Naval Command and **HSL** (Hindustan Shipyard Limited). The **ISRO** (Indian Space Research Organisation) spaceport, the **Satish Dhawan Space Centre (SDSC-SHAR)**, is at Sriharikota. In rural governance, **Dubbiganipalli** was named among India's Best Village Panchayats (November 2025).

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Pawan Kalyan inducted into Takeda Shingen Clan (Jan 2026) as 'Tiger of Martial Arts', Fifth Dan.
- Padma Awards 2026: Garimella Balakrishna Prasad (Posthumous, AP) in Art.

- DRDO NSTL Visakhapatnam unveiled a man-portable autonomous underwater system (Nov 2025).
- ISRO's Satish Dhawan Space Centre is at Sriharikota, AP; Dubbiganipalli named a Best Village Panchayat (Nov 2025).

items.title: AP current-affairs timeline (Nov 2025 → Sep 2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** AP current-affairs timeline (Nov 2025 → Sep 2026).

A month-by-month map of exam-relevant Andhra Pradesh events across the coverage window, with why each matters.

| Month | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| Nov 2025 | 30th CII Partnership Summit (14-15 Nov, Visakhapatnam); Rythanna Meekosam launched (24 Nov); NSTL autonomous underwater system; Dubbiganipalli among Best Village Panchayats | Summit venue/host and the farm-scheme launch date are frequent single-fact questions |
| Dec 2025 | 87th Senior National Badminton Championships (Vijayawada) — Surya Charishma Tamiri wins; ISRO launches from SDSC-SHAR; **Markapuram and Polavaram districts formed (31 Dec), taking AP to 28 districts** | The jump to 28 districts is the most-tested administrative change |
| Jan 2026 | Pawan Kalyan honoured 'Tiger of Martial Arts'; Padma Awards (AP in Art); ASC ARJUN Rail Robocop at Visakhapatnam (22 Jan); AP EDB-FLO Women Entrepreneurs' Industrial Park MoU; Bank of Baroda report — AP tops FY26 investment | 'Who/where' recall plus the investment-ranking fact |
| Feb 2026 | **AP Budget 2026-27 presented (14 Feb) by Finance Minister Payyavula Keshav** | Budget date and minister are standard questions |
| Apr 2026 | Polavaram new diaphragm wall done (2 Apr); INS Aridhaman commissioned (3 Apr); Amaravati sole-capital assent (6 Apr); Quantum Valley 1S/1Q testbeds (14 Apr); INS Taragiri commissioned | A dense cluster of exact dates examiners love to shuffle |
| Jun 2026 | South Coast Railway zone operational (1 Jun), HQ Visakhapatnam | Newest railway zone and its HQ |
| Aug 2026 | Bhogapuram airport opens (17 Aug); Reliance UCG complex proposed for Eluru (20 Aug); Veligonda inaugurated (31 Aug) | Airport opening date is high-yield |

**MoU** = Memorandum of Understanding; **UCG** = Underground Coal Gasification. **Remember it:** April 2026 packs four milestones — Polavaram wall (2nd), INS Aridhaman (3rd), Amaravati assent (6th), Quantum testbeds (14th).

### In short

**TL;DR**

- AP crossed to 28 districts on 31 Dec 2025 with Markapuram and Polavaram.
- AP Budget 2026-27 was presented on 14 February 2026 by FM Payyavula Keshav.
- April 2026 clustered four milestones: Polavaram wall (2), INS Aridhaman (3), Amaravati assent (6), Quantum testbeds (14).
- South Coast Railway zone became operational on 1 June 2026 (HQ Visakhapatnam).
- August 2026: Bhogapuram airport (17), Reliance UCG proposal (20), Veligonda inauguration (31).

items.title: AP Budget 2026-27 at a glance
items.body:
**In one line.** The size and spending priorities of Andhra Pradesh's 2026-27 state budget.

**Why it is asked.** The presenter, the date and the largest allocation head are standard budget questions; the deficit figures test whether you can read a budget table.

The **Andhra Pradesh Budget 2026-27** was presented on **14 February 2026** by Finance Minister **Payyavula Keshav**. (**GSDP** below means Gross State Domestic Product — the total value of goods and services produced in the state in a year.)

| Aggregate | 2026-27 |
|---|---|
| GSDP (current prices) | ₹19,75,073 crore (about 12% growth) |
| Total expenditure (excluding debt repayment) | ₹3,10,058 crore (12% over revised 2025-26) |
| Fiscal deficit | 3.8% of GSDP (₹75,868 crore) |
| Revenue deficit | 1.1% of GSDP (₹22,003 crore) |

**Major sectoral allocations**

| Head | Allocation |
|---|---|
| Education, Sports, Arts & Culture | ₹35,673 crore |
| Health & Family Welfare | ₹19,630 crore |
| Agriculture & Allied Activities | ₹14,433 crore |
| Annadata Sukhibhava (scheme) | ₹6,600 crore |
| Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust | ₹4,000 crore |

The largest rises in capital spending were for **irrigation and flood control, water supply and sanitation, and urban development**. GSDP in 2025-26 was about ₹17.62 trillion (around 10% growth).

**Don't confuse.** The **fiscal deficit** (total borrowing need, 3.8%) is larger than the **revenue deficit** (shortfall on day-to-day account, 1.1%); options often swap the two.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- AP Budget 2026-27 presented 14 Feb 2026 by FM Payyavula Keshav.
- GSDP 2026-27 projected at Rs 19,75,073 crore (~12% growth); total expenditure Rs 3,10,058 crore.
- Fiscal deficit targeted 3.8% of GSDP; revenue deficit 1.1% of GSDP.
- Education/Sports/Arts/Culture got Rs 35,673 crore — the largest of the listed heads.
- Annadata Sukhibhava Rs 6,600 crore; Dr NTR Vaidya Seva Trust Rs 4,000 crore.

items.title: AP defence, space & quantum installations (2025–26)
items.body:
**In one line.** The national defence, space and quantum facilities that Andhra Pradesh hosts, mostly around Visakhapatnam and Amaravati.

**Why it is asked.** 'Which asset is where / when commissioned' are easy map-and-date questions, and the two submarines plus two quantum items are easy to mix up.

**SSBN** below means a nuclear-powered submarine that carries ballistic missiles (ship-submersible-ballistic-nuclear); **DRDO**, **ISRO** and **HSL** are defined in an earlier note.

| Asset | Location | What happened (2025-26) |
|---|---|---|
| **INS Aridhaman** | Visakhapatnam | India's 3rd SSBN; commissioned 3 Apr 2026 |
| **INS Taragiri** | Visakhapatnam | 5th Project 17A stealth frigate (built by Mazagon Dock, about 75% indigenous); commissioned Apr 2026 |
| **NSTL (DRDO)** | Visakhapatnam | Naval-systems lab; unveiled a man-portable autonomous underwater system (Nov 2025) |
| **Eastern Naval Command / HSL** | Visakhapatnam | Main east-coast naval hub and shipyard |
| **SDSC-SHAR (ISRO)** | Sriharikota | India's spaceport for PSLV, GSLV and LVM3 rockets |
| **Quantum Valley 1S/1Q testbeds** | Amaravati / Gannavaram | Inaugurated 14 Apr 2026 (World Quantum Day); first state Quantum Test Reference Facility |
| **Quantum Valley Tech Park** | Amaravati | IBM + TCS + IIT Madras — India's largest quantum computer |

**Don't confuse.** **INS Aridhaman** is a *submarine* (3rd SSBN); **INS Taragiri** is a *frigate* (5th Project 17A) — both at Visakhapatnam, commissioned in April 2026.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- INS Aridhaman (3rd SSBN) commissioned at Visakhapatnam on 3 April 2026.
- INS Taragiri (5th Project 17A frigate) commissioned at Visakhapatnam in April 2026, ~75% indigenous.
- DRDO's NSTL, Visakhapatnam unveiled a man-portable autonomous underwater system (Nov 2025).
- ISRO's spaceport SDSC-SHAR is at Sriharikota; Visakhapatnam hosts the Eastern Naval Command and HSL.
- Amaravati Quantum Valley 1S/1Q testbeds were inaugurated on 14 April 2026; Tech Park partners are IBM, TCS and IIT Madras.

items.title: AP 'Super Six' & welfare schemes — names, amounts, launch (2024–26)
items.body:
**In one line.** The exact names, benefits and launch dates of AP's 'Super Six' and related welfare schemes, and the older schemes they replaced.

**Why it is asked.** Examiners pair the new scheme with the old one it replaced, so you must know both names; benefit amounts are common single-fact questions.

The **NDA (TDP-JSP-BJP)** government (from June 2024) renamed several YSRCP-era schemes and rolled out the **'Super Six'** guarantees. (**LPG** = liquefied petroleum gas, that is, cooking-gas cylinders; **PM-KISAN** is the central farmer-income scheme; **CKD** = chronic kidney disease; **PwD** = persons with disabilities; **RTC** = Road Transport Corporation buses.)

| Scheme (new) | Benefit | Replaces |
|---|---|---|
| **Thalliki Vandanam** | ₹15,000 a year per school child, paid through the mother; launched Jun 2025 | Amma Vodi |
| **Annadata Sukhibhava** | ₹20,000 a year per farmer family (₹6,000 PM-KISAN + ₹14,000 State) | YSR Rythu Bharosa |
| **NTR Bharosa Pensions** | ₹4,000 a month general; ₹6,000 disabled; up to ₹15,000 bedridden/CKD; enhanced Jul 2024 | YSR Pension Kanuka |
| **Deepam 2.0** | 3 free LPG cylinders a year to about 1.08 crore households | upgrades Deepam |
| **Stree Shakti** | Free non-AC RTC bus travel for women; launched 15 Aug 2025; extended to PwD | — |
| **Matsyakara Bharosa** | Livelihood support for fishermen | — |

In July 2026, Thalliki Vandanam credited ₹10,120.78 crore to 42.70 lakh mothers (67.47 lakh students).

**Don't confuse.** Thalliki Vandanam replaced *Amma Vodi*; Annadata Sukhibhava replaced *YSR Rythu Bharosa* — do not swap the old names.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Thalliki Vandanam — ₹15,000/yr per child via mother (Jun 2025); replaces Amma Vodi.
- Annadata Sukhibhava — ₹20,000/yr = ₹6,000 PM-KISAN + ₹14,000 State; replaces YSR Rythu Bharosa.
- NTR Bharosa Pensions — ₹4,000 general / ₹6,000 disabled / up to ₹15,000 bedridden; replaces YSR Pension Kanuka.

items.title: AP vision, governance initiatives & 2025–26 administrative changes
items.body:
**In one line.** Andhra Pradesh's long-term vision, its digital-governance tools, and the 2025-26 changes to districts and police zones.

**Why it is asked.** The vision names ('Padi Sutralu', P4), the district reorganisation and the zilla-parishad date are frequently tested, and the 'is Madanapalle a district?' point is a planted trap.

**Vision and anti-poverty.** *Swarna Andhra @2047* (launched November 2024) aims for a wealthy, healthy and happy AP by 2047, built on ten principles called 'Padi Sutralu' (zero poverty, employment, skilling, water and energy security, deep-tech growth). *P4* stands for **Public-Private-People Partnership**: the top 10% of citizens, the 'Margadarsis', support the bottom 20%, the 'Bangaru Kutumbalu', aiming for zero poverty by 2029.

**Digital governance.** *Mana Mitra*, a WhatsApp service (launched 30 January 2025; number 9552300009), grew from 161 to 700 services by 15 August 2025 — certificates, bill payments, temple bookings. The **RTGS** (Real Time Governance Society) was revived under IT Minister Nara Lokesh.

**Administrative changes.** Districts rose from 26 to 28 on 31 December 2025 — new **Polavaram** (headquarters Rampachodavaram, carved from Alluri Sitharama Raju district) and **Markapuram** (headquarters Markapuram, carved from Prakasam). **Madanapalle** is the headquarters of **Annamayya** district, not a separate district — the proposed '29th district' was never notified. The state moved to **28 zilla parishads** on 25 September 2026. New revenue divisions (31 December 2025): Rampachodavaram, Markapuram, Kanigiri. In September 2026 the Cabinet approved four new police commissionerates (including Guntur, Kurnool and Rajamahendravaram).

**Don't confuse.** Madanapalle is only the *headquarters* of Annamayya district — it is not itself the 29th district.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Swarna Andhra @2047 — launched Nov 2024; ten 'Padi Sutralu'; wealthy/healthy/happy AP by 2047.
- P4 (Public-Private-People Partnership) — Margadarsis (top 10%) support Bangaru Kutumbalu (bottom 20%); zero poverty by 2029.
- Mana Mitra — WhatsApp governance from 30 Jan 2025; 161→700 services (15 Aug 2025). RTGS revived under Nara Lokesh.
- 28 districts with effect from 31 Dec 2025 — Polavaram (HQ Rampachodavaram), Markapuram (HQ Markapuram); Madanapalle = HQ of Annamayya, not a district.
- 28 zilla parishads from 25 Sep 2026; four new police commissionerates approved Sep 2026 (Guntur, Kurnool, Rajamahendravaram).

items.title: AP key events month-by-month (Oct 2025 → Sep 2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** A single chronological recap of the highest-yield Andhra Pradesh events from October 2025 to September 2026.

**Why it is asked.** APPSC loves 'which event happened in which month' questions; this ledger ties each event to why it is likely to be set.

| Month | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| Oct 2025 | Cyclone Montha formed about 24 Oct; landfall near Kakinada on the night of 28-29 Oct (winds 90-100 kmph); 3 deaths, about 1.8 million people affected across 249 mandals, crops flattened over about 87,000 hectares | Disaster facts (name, landfall point, scale) are common |
| Nov 2025 | 30th CII Partnership Summit, AU Engineering Grounds Visakhapatnam (14-15 Nov), inaugurated by Vice-President C. P. Radhakrishnan — 613 MoUs worth ₹13,25,716 crore, about 16,31,188 jobs | Summit host and MoU value are favourite figures |
| Dec 2025 | Ponduru Khadi (Srikakulam) gets a GI tag (Geographical Indication); Cabinet ratifies ₹7,387 crore Amaravati loan, 10% road cess, DA (dearness allowance) hike | GI-tag products of AP are regularly asked |
| Jan 2026 | NITI Fiscal Health Index — AP in the bottom five (Odisha No.1); Investment Friendliness Index — AP 6th among large states (8th overall); Padma Awards 2026 announced (131 awardees) | Index ranks and the Padma count |
| Feb 2026 | Budget 2026-27 presented 14 Feb by FM Payyavula Keshav, outlay ₹3,32,205 crore; School Education highest allocation about ₹32,308 crore; about ₹6,000 crore to Amaravati; three City Economic Regions | Budget date, presenter and top head |
| Mar 2026 | Cabinet gives a 50% one-time waiver of interest on property-tax arrears for 2025-26 (deadline 31 Mar) | Policy-decision recall |
| Apr 2026 | Google broke ground on a US$15 billion AI data-centre hub, Visakhapatnam (about 28 Apr); Cabinet cleared 34 proposals (aviation policy, organ-transplant law, revised Polavaram funding); AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act 2026 — Amaravati sole capital, Presidential assent 6 Apr; Justice Lisa Gill sworn in as 5th Chief Justice of AP High Court (25 Apr) | Capital-status date and the new Chief Justice |
| May 2026 | Omnibus Ease of Doing Business Act 2026 and Pedestrian Safety Policy; 33.33% BC (Backward Classes) quota in ULBs plus direct election of Mayors/chairpersons; 16th Finance Commission gives ₹28,785 crore to AP local bodies (2026-31) | Law and quota reforms |
| Jun 2026 | Rules issued for direct election of Mayors and municipal chairpersons; SEC (State Election Commissioner) A. C. Punetha directed readiness for 2026 local-body polls | Election-administration recall |
| Jul 2026 | Thalliki Vandanam ₹10,120.78 crore credited to about 42.70 lakh mothers, about 67.47 lakh students | Scheme-disbursement figure |
| Aug 2026 | PM Modi inaugurated Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram (1 Aug; ₹5,640 crore, built by GMR, 6 million passengers a year) — projects worth ₹17,900 crore+ dedicated; commercial operations shifted from Visakhapatnam to Bhogapuram on 17 Aug | Airport inauguration vs operations dates |
| Sep 2026 | Cabinet approved four new Police Commissionerates (Guntur, Kurnool, Rajamahendravaram and one more), revised HNSS (Handri-Neeva Sujala Sravanthi) sanction about ₹463.55 crore, and 815 Junior Assistant posts | Governance decisions |

**Appointments 2026:** Chief Justice, AP High Court = Justice Lisa Gill; Chief Secretary = G. Sai Prasad (from 1 Mar); APPSC Chairperson = A. R. Anuradha (retired IPS).

**Don't confuse.** The airport was *inaugurated* on 1 August 2026 but commercial *operations* shifted there only on 17 August 2026.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- Oct 2025: Cyclone Montha formed ~24 Oct; landfall near Kakinada night of 28–29 Oct (winds 90–100 kmph); 3 deaths, ~1.8M affected across 249 mandals, crops flattened over ~87,000 ha.
- Nov 2025: 30th CII Partnership Summit, AU Engineering Grounds Visakhapatnam (14–15 Nov), inaugurated by VP C. P. Radhakrishnan — 613 MoUs worth ₹13,25,716 cr, ~16,31,188 jobs.
- Dec 2025: Ponduru Khadi (Srikakulam) gets GI tag; Cabinet ratifies ₹7,387 cr Amaravati loan, 10% road cess, DA hike.
- Jan 2026: NITI Fiscal Health Index — AP in bottom five (Odisha No.1); Investment Friendliness Index — AP 6th (large states)/8th overall; Padma Awards 2026 announced (131 awardees).
- Feb 2026: Budget 2026-27 presented 14 Feb by FM Payyavula Keshav, outlay ₹3,32,205 cr; School Education highest allocation ~₹32,308 cr; ~₹6,000 cr to Amaravati; three City Economic Regions.
- Mar 2026: Cabinet 50% one-time waiver of interest on property-tax arrears 2025-26 (deadline 31 Mar).
- Apr 2026: Google broke ground on US$15bn AI data-centre hub, Visakhapatnam (~28 Apr); Cabinet cleared 34 proposals (aviation policy, organ-transplant law, revised Polavaram funding); AP Reorganisation (Amendment) Act 2026 — Amaravati sole capital, Presidential assent 6 Apr; Justice Lisa Gill sworn in as 5th CJ of AP High Court (25 Apr).
- May 2026: Omnibus Ease of Doing Business Act 2026 + Pedestrian Safety Policy; 33.33% BC quota in ULBs + direct election of Mayors/chairpersons; 16th Finance Commission ₹28,785 cr to AP local bodies (2026-31).
- Jun 2026: Rules issued for direct election of Mayors/municipal chairpersons; SEC A. C. Punetha directed readiness for 2026 local body polls.
- Jul 2026: Talliki Vandanam ₹10,120.78 cr credited to ~42.70 lakh mothers, ~67.47 lakh students.
- Aug 2026: PM Modi inaugurated Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport, Bhogapuram (1 Aug; ₹5,640 cr, GMR, 6M pax/yr) — projects worth ₹17,900 cr+ dedicated; commercial ops shifted Vizag→Bhogapuram 17 Aug.
- Sep 2026: Cabinet approved four new Police Commissionerates (Guntur, Kurnool, Rajamahendravaram +1), HNSS revised sanction ~₹463.55 cr, and 815 Junior Assistant posts.

items.title: AP current-affairs timeline — recent additions (Jun-Oct 2026)
items.body:
**In one line.** The latest Andhra Pradesh developments carried in this bank, filling the thin June and September-October 2026 windows.

**Why it is asked.** The APPSC Group-1 Notification 07/2026 details (vacancies and dates) are directly exam-relevant to candidates and appear as factual questions. Current affairs in this app are updated through **9 October 2026**.

| Month | What happened | Why it matters for the exam |
|---|---|---|
| **Jun 2026** | South Coast Railway (SCoR) zone becomes operational (1 Jun), headquartered at Visakhapatnam | India's newest railway zone; HQ city is a common one-mark fact |
| **Aug 2026** | Alluri Sitarama Raju International Airport (Bhogapuram) opens for commercial operations (17 Aug); Veligonda Project inaugurated | New airport opening date is high-yield |
| **Oct 2026** | APPSC Group-1 **Notification 07/2026** released (6 Oct) for 166 vacancies; Screening Test set for 24 Jan 2027; online applications close 27 Oct 2026 | Notification date, vacancy count and the application window are directly testable |

**Standing AP facts worth revising:** GSDP 2025-26 was about ₹17.62 trillion; the Economic Survey 2024-25 rated AP the 'leading performer' in agriculture (about 8.8% growth); Nagarjunasagar-Srisailam is India's largest tiger reserve; Kolleru and Coringa are Ramsar wetlands (internationally important wetland sites); Seshachalam is a biosphere reserve.

**Remember it:** Notification 07/2026 = 166 vacancies, released 6 Oct 2026, apply by 27 Oct 2026, Screening on 24 Jan 2027.

### In short

**The story in brief.** The background, the cause-and-effect and every term used are explained in the sections above; the essential facts to carry into the exam are these.

**TL;DR**

- SCoR railway zone operational 1 Jun 2026, HQ Visakhapatnam.
- Bhogapuram (Alluri Sitarama Raju) International Airport opened 17 Aug 2026.
- APPSC Group-1 Notification 07/2026 released 6 Oct 2026; 166 vacancies; Screening 24 Jan 2027.
- Group-1 online application deadline: 27 Oct 2026.
- AP GSDP 2025-26 ≈ ₹17.62 trillion; agriculture “leading performer” (~8.8%).
